kl_example.note: Exact two-action KL only; real LLM training uses token-level implementation-specific estimators. Old rollout policy and reference policy serve distinct roles.

paired_experiment.controls: Same four tasks, outcome categories and total attempt budget of 4, assumed common evaluation and cost accounting. Rounds include the initial generation/execution attempt; repair-only rounds equal rounds minus one. Categories alone do not prove full quality equivalence. Not all tasks are established initial failures, so 2/4 is not a repair-success rate.
paired_experiment.conclusion: Same assumed confirmed pass rate 2/4, all-task rounds 2.75 -> 2.00, pass-task rounds 2.50 -> 1.00, cost 330 -> 240 hypothetical units. Failed/unknown costs remain counted.
paired_experiment.reward_rule: No cost penalty formula selected. Unknown has no semantic score; keep it separate. Prefer reducing cost subject to quality and evidence constraints, not buying a higher number by dropping hard tasks.

learner_checks: C: positive advantage at ratio 1.5 has a flat scalar surrogate; why is stronger probability growth not always rewarded?
D: same pass/fail/unknown outcomes but lower rounds/cost: what improved, and can we claim accuracy rose?
